questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In remote sensing and GIS, georeferencing is the process of assigning what to an unreferenced raster image?
options: Assigning real-world coordinates to raster images
Removing atmospheric scattering from optical satellite scenes
Classifying land cover using supervised training samples
Combining multiple images into a single seamless mosaic
questions.solution: Georeferencing: GCPs + polynomial transformation.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In sequence stratigraphy, the systems tracts LST, TST, and HST are recognized by their characteristic what?
options: LST: transgressive retrogradational parasequences backstepping across the exposed shelf edge and lowstand plain
LST (lowstand, basin floor fan + slope fan), TST (transgressive, retrogradational parasequences), HST (highstand, progradational)
HST: retrogradational backstepping of the shoreline facies belts with aggradational parasequence stacking throughout the entire tract
TST: progradational coarsening-upward shoreface parasequences with forced regression at the top of the tract
questions.solution: Sequence: between two unconformities. Parasequence: flooding surface-bound.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: An isomorphous series in mineralogy refers to minerals that share which common property?
options: Minerals with same structure but different composition (e.g., olivine: forsterite-fayalite)
No series. Mineral composition is always fixed and never varies continuously
Same composition different structure. A single formula yields several distinct minerals
Different composition different structure. No structural link exists between related species
questions.solution: Complete solid solution: olivine (Mg-Fe), plagioclase (Na-Ca), garnet. Limited: pyroxene.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A downward (trough-shaped) fold, with the youngest beds in its core, is a:
questions.solution: A syncline sags downward; limbs dip toward the axis and youngest rocks lie in the core.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The D″ layer just above the core-mantle boundary is characterized by which features such as ULVZs and the post-perovskite phase?
options: Outer core. A 200-300 km thick zone of iron alloy resting directly beneath the lower mantle
Inner core. A thin shell of solid iron that generates the Earth's dipole field and completely stops S-waves
~200-300 km thick. ULVZ (ultra-low velocity zones). Post-perovskite phase. Seismic anisotropy
Upper mantle. A shallow zone of partial melt responsible for low-velocity anomalies
questions.solution: D″: thermal boundary layer. Partial melt? LLSVP (large low shear velocity provinces).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: On the Mohs hardness scale, quartz is assigned which hardness value?
questions.solution: Mohs scale: talc(1) to diamond(10). Quartz = 7.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A mineral has passed through 2 half-lives of an isotope whose half-life is 5.73 (in the given time units). Its age is:
questions.solution: Age = number of half-lives × half-life = 2×5.73 = 11.46.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A brownfield site, an abandoned or underused industrial property, must be subjected to what before redevelopment?
options: Only a structural survey of existing buildings
Only a geophysical survey of the basement
questions.solution: Brownfield: formerly developed land, potentially contaminated. Phase I (desk study), Phase II (sampling) required.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Electrical resistivity tomography (ERT) inversion:
options: Treats measured apparent resistivities as the final subsurface image
Converts apparent resistivities with no iterative modelling step
Smooths the data without relating it to a layered earth model
Converts apparent resistivity data to true resistivity model
questions.solution: Inversion: iterative. Minimize difference between observed and modeled. Smoothness constraints.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A hardground in a carbonate sequence represents which synsedimentary diagenetic condition?
options: Deep burial diagenesis after complete lithification
Contact metamorphism by an intruding sill
Glacial erosion and striation of bedrock
questions.solution: Hardground: lithified sea floor during sedimentation. Often bored, encrusted. Represents hiatus in deposition.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: How is shale, a common fine-grained sedimentary rock, best defined?
options: Carbonate rock composed of microcrystalline calcite mud and lime
Coarse-grained rock composed of well-rounded quartz sand grains
Volcaniclastic rock made of welded glass shards and pumice fragments
questions.solution: Shale: most abundant sedimentary rock. Low permeability — hydrocarbon source rock.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which of the following correctly describes fault gouge and its occurrence within a brittle fault zone?
options: Coarse breccia of angular wall-rock fragments
Undeformed sedimentary fill of a graben
Lava flow brecciated during surface eruption
questions.solution: Fault gouge: very fine-grained, clay-rich. Forms in upper crust. Acts as barrier to fluid flow. Important in petroleum geology.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is the intermediate volcanic rock composed mainly of plagioclase plus hornblende or pyroxene?
options: Mafic volcanic rock composed of olivine, pyroxene and calcic plagioclase
Ultramafic volcanic rock consisting chiefly of olivine with minor chromite
Felsic volcanic rock made of quartz, alkali feldspar and minor biotite
questions.solution: Andesite: named after Andes. Common in subduction zone volcanoes.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The garnet-biotite geothermometer estimates temperature on the basis of which exchange reaction?
options: Ti-in-quartz thermometer calibrated for very high-grade metapelites and granulite facies rocks
Calcite-dolomite solvus thermometer used for impure marbles to estimate peak metamorphic temperature
Garnet-clinopyroxene geothermometer applied to eclogite and granulite facies assemblages
Fe-Mg exchange between Grt-Bt. Ferry and Spear (1978). T estimate from K_D = (Fe/Mg)_Grt/(Fe/Mg)_Bt
questions.solution: Garnet-biotite: lnK_D ≈ (C₁)/(T) + C₂. Calibrated experimentally. Pressure from GASP, GRAIL.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In GIS, the buffer analysis tool generates what at a specified distance around points, lines, or polygon features?
options: Zones of specified distance around features
Zones of equal elevation around a reference point
Linear paths between two or more chosen destination points
Grid cells sharing the same thematic attribute value
questions.solution: Buffer: creates zone of distance around features.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Reservoir quality prediction depends mainly on which factors controlling porosity and permeability with depth?
options: Independent of burial depth because porosity is controlled solely by the original grain size of the sand
Depth (porosity loss), mineralogy (Quartz vs lithic), compaction. Contact cement vs pore-filling
Always high because burial never reduces reservoir porosity significantly
No prediction possible because diagenesis is entirely random in all basins
questions.solution: Porosity: sandstone ~0.5%/100m loss. Lithic arenite: rapid compaction. Qtz arenite: deeper potential.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: To which silicate group of minerals does the mineral hornblende belong?
options: Mica group (sheet silicate with basal cleavage)
questions.solution: Hornblende — amphibole. 56° and 124° cleavage. Common in andesite.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Bowen's reaction series predicts that the first silicate mineral to crystallize from a cooling basaltic magma is:
questions.solution: In the discontinuous series olivine crystallizes first at the highest temperature; quartz last.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A coal seam covers 5 km², is 5 m thick, with density 1.3 t/m³. The in-situ reserve is about:
questions.solution: Reserve = area×thickness×density = 5×10⁶ m²×5 m×1.3 t/m³ ≈ 32.5 Mt.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Subduction zone: oceanic plate subducts beneath continental plate creates:
options: Mountain belt formed by collision of two continental masses
Volcanic arc, trench, accretionary prism, back-arc basin
Zone of new oceanic crust formed at a divergent plate boundary
Graben structure produced by continental extension and stretching
questions.solution: Subduction: Andes-type. Ocean-continent. Mariana-type: ocean-ocean. Deep trench, Wadati-Benioff zone.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Core-mantle boundary (D double prime) is:
options: The boundary between crust and mantle
questions.solution: D double prime: lowermost 200 km. Ultra-low velocity zones.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What characteristics should a good index (guide) fossil possess?
options: Widespread but short-lived in geologic time
Rare and confined to a single basin with an extremely long stratigraphic range
Found in igneous and metamorphic rocks, permitting absolute-age dating of plutons
Geographically restricted to one locality but present in almost every rock formation there
questions.solution: Wide distribution plus a short time range makes a fossil useful for correlation/dating.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is the coarse-grained plutonic rock that is the equivalent of basalt?
options: Coarse-grained intrusive rock that is the plutonic equivalent of rhyolite
Fine-grained volcanic rock with the same composition as diorite and tonalite
Medium-grained intrusive rock consisting mainly of quartz and K-feldspar
questions.solution: Gabbro: plutonic mafic. Plagioclase + pyroxene ± olivine.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Using a simplified proxy where calorific value ≈ 70 × fixed-carbon%, a coal with 70% fixed carbon has a calorific value of about:
questions.solution: CV ≈ 70 × 70 = 4900 kcal/kg (illustrative proxy).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The theory that the Earth's lithosphere is divided into moving plates is:
questions.solution: Plate tectonics explains earthquakes, volcanism and mountain building by plate interactions.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which statement about ore and gangue is correct?
options: Gangue is the high-grade metal-bearing concentrate recovered during smelting
Gangue is the portion of the deposit that carries the recoverable metal value
Gangue is the worthless mineral matter associated with the ore
Ore minerals have no commercial value and are discarded with the waste rock
questions.solution: The ore mineral carries the metal of value; the surrounding gangue is discarded or processed away.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What sequence of events and phases characterise the Himalayan orogeny in the geological record?
options: Silurian continental collision between the Gondwana cratons of India and Africa and the closure of an early ocean
Tethys closure, India-Asia collision (~55 Ma). Three phases: Eo-Himalayan, Neo-Himalayan
Precambrian assembly of the Indian Shield before the opening of the Tethys ocean basin
A single continuous uplift without any break since the Archean era in the whole region
questions.solution: Himalaya: Main Central Thrust (MCT), Main Boundary Thrust (MBT), Main Frontal Thrust (MFT).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which option correctly describes the shape, sediment distribution and setting of an alluvial fan?
options: Flat, low-lying area alongside a river that is inundated during floods
Low ridge of sediment built along the channel bank during flood events
Fan-shaped sediment body deposited where a river enters a standing body of water
Cone-shaped deposit at mountain front. Coarse near apex, fine at toe
questions.solution: Alluvial fan: flash floods, debris flows. Bajada: coalescing fans.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In a normal fault, how does the hanging wall move relative to the footwall, and what is its typical range of dip?
options: Hanging wall moves up relative to the footwall, driven by regional compression
Both blocks slide horizontally with no vertical movement and a near-vertical fault plane
Hanging wall moves down relative to footwall (extension). Dip 45-90°
Footwall drops relative to the hanging wall, with fault plane dipping less than 45°
questions.solution: Normal fault: extensional tectonics. Graben (down-dropped block) and horst (uplifted block).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Core composition: iron-nickel alloy with light elements (S, O, Si):
options: No light elements. The outer core is pure iron with no measurable density deficit
Light elements explain density deficit of outer core (~5-10%) vs pure iron
Only nickel is present, and it fully accounts for the observed density of the outer core
Only pure iron. Nickel and light elements are confined to the mantle and crust
questions.solution: Outer core density ~10% less than pure Fe at core conditions. Light elements: S, O, Si, H.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Banded iron formation records precipitation of what materials, and in which type of environment?
options: Precipitation of iron and silica from seawater
Metamorphic segregation of iron from mafic host rocks
Submarine volcanic eruption of iron-rich lava flows
Biological fixation of iron by ancient photosynthetic organisms
questions.solution: BIF: alternating iron-rich and silica-rich layers. ~2.5-1.8 Ga.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In marine seismic surveying, an air gun source produces what kind of signal in the water?
options: Pressure pulse (bubble oscillation). Tow cable with hydrophones
A continuous tonal sweep emitted while the streamer is being towed astern
Only electromagnetic signals recorded by nodes on the sea floor
Static electric discharge needing no compressed air at the source array
questions.solution: Air gun: compressed air release. Bubble oscillation produces primary pulse. Hydrophone streamer.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The metamorphic aureole is the zone of contact metamorphism that forms around an:
options: Zone of weathering and alteration around an exposed outcrop of rock
Regional zone of high-grade metamorphism across an entire mountain belt
Zone of contact metamorphism around intrusion. Width: meters to km
Zone of shearing and mylonitization adjacent to a major fault plane
questions.solution: Aureole: inner zone (pyroxene hornfels), outer zone (spotted slate).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Regional metamorphism, affecting large areas, is characteristically associated with which tectonic setting?
options: Local heating by magma at shallow depths in narrow contact aureoles
Impact cratering producing coesite and stishovite at the surface
Mountain belt (orogenic). High P/T. Large areas
Hot seawater circulation altering basalts along mid-ocean ridges
questions.solution: Regional: convergent margins. P-T gradient: Barrovian (medium) or Buchan (high T/low P).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Migmatite: partial melting of crust. Leucosome = granitic melt. Melosome (restite) =:
options: Granitic melt that has migrated away from the source region
Volcanic glass quenched rapidly on the seafloor surface
Felsic fraction that crystallized first from the partial melt
questions.solution: Leucosome: felsic melt fraction. Melosome: mafic residue. Melanosome: dark, mafic-rich.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Metamorphic P-T path: clockwise vs counterclockwise:
options: Both clockwise and counterclockwise paths record identical thermal histories
Clockwise: heating followed by exhumation. Counterclockwise: thickening followed by heating
Clockwise: thickening → heating → exhumation. Counterclockwise: heating → thickening
Clockwise: isobaric heating. Counterclockwise: isothermal decompression
questions.solution: Clockwise: typical continental collision. Counterclockwise: magmatic underplating, arc setting.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Amphibolite facies: T = 500-700C. Minerals:
options: Pyroxene + garnet + plagioclase with no hydrous minerals at all
questions.solution: Amphibolite: moderate to high grade. Basalt: hornblende + plagioclase. Pelite: garnet + staurolite + kyanite.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A gravity anomaly measured over a body that is denser than its surroundings will be:
options: Positive only when the body outcrops at surface
Negative, since dense rocks give a gravity low
Zero, since density never affects gravity
questions.solution: Positive anomaly: dense body attracts. Negative: less dense. Bouguer anomaly corrects for terrain, elevation, latitude.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Mississippi Valley-type Pb-Zn deposits are characteristically hosted in which rock type and formed at what temperature?
options: Magmatic segregation of immiscible sulfide melts in a layered mafic intrusion
Volcanic-hosted exhalative ore accumulated on the ancient seafloor
Porphyry-style stockwork mineralization with a potassic alteration core
Carbonate-hosted. Sphalerite + galena. Low temperature. Not volcanic
questions.solution: MVT: epigenetic, in limestone/dolomite. Solution collapse breccia. Viburnum Trend (Missouri).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The K-Ar dating method, based on ⁴⁰K decaying to ⁴⁰Ar by electron capture, is applicable to which K-bearing minerals?
options: Rb-Sr method applied to whole-rock samples of the igneous body that is being dated, giving model and isochron ages in detail
⁴⁰K → ⁴⁰Ar (electron capture, EC). T½ = 1.25 Ga. For K-bearing minerals (biotite, muscovite, K-feldspar, glauconite)
C-14 method for recently formed organic material and charcoals of a young age
U-Pb method applied to zircon, monazite and titanite crystals of the same rock
questions.solution: K-Ar: argon retention T ~300°C. Closure T different for each mineral. ⁴⁰Ar/³⁹Ar = variant.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A bed drops 20 m over a horizontal distance of 10 m. Its dip angle is about:
questions.solution: dip = tan⁻¹(rise/run) = tan⁻¹(20/10) ≈ 63.4°.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A coal sample (proximate analysis) has 5% moisture, 20% volatile matter and 15% ash. Its fixed carbon is:
questions.solution: Fixed C = 100 − (moisture + VM + ash) = 100 − (5+20+15) = 60%.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The Darcy velocity of groundwater flow through a porous medium is defined as the:
options: Volumetric flow rate per unit cross-sectional area
Actual speed of a water particle moving through the pores
Total discharge divided by the effective porosity of the medium
Ratio of the hydraulic gradient to the hydraulic conductivity
questions.solution: q = Q/A = Ki. Apparent velocity through total area.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which of the following correctly represents the general chemical formula of the mineral tourmaline?
options: K(Mg,Fe)₃AlSi₃O₁₀(OH)₂ — hydrous aluminosilicate of the mica group
questions.solution: Tourmaline: complex borosilicate. Wide solid solution. Schorl (Fe), elbaite (Li,Na), dravite (Mg).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which of the following correctly describes the dark coating that forms on rock surfaces in arid regions?
options: Vitreous silica glaze precipitated on rock surfaces by dew and fog
Thin deposit of wind-blown clay smeared across the rock surface
Hard crust of calcium carbonate formed below the soil surface
Mn-Fe oxide coating on rock surfaces in arid environments
questions.solution: Varnish: MnO₂, Fe₂O₃. Dark coating. Used for relative dating. Rock art surfaces.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Sentinel-2 MSI: 13 bands, 10m resolution in visible and NIR. Best for vegetation analysis:
questions.solution: Sentinel-2: 10m in B2,B3,B4,B8. 20m in B5-B7,B8A,B11,B12. 60m in B1,B9,B10.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is the main purpose of cement grouting in fractured rock, and which types are used?
options: Grout is used only to raise the temperature of the surrounding rock mass before blasting work
Cement grout dissolves fractures and increases rock permeability for drainage
Cement grout → fill fractures, reduce permeability. Consolidation vs curtain grouting
Grouting is confined to muck filling of the excavation after blasting
questions.solution: Grouting: pressure grouting. Water-cement ratio 0.5:1 to 5:1. Lugeon test for permeability.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which ultramafic, potassic rock is the primary source rock for diamonds?
options: Felsic volcanic rock rich in quartz that forms continental flood provinces
Ultramafic potassic rock. Source rock for diamonds
Mafic volcanic rock composed of plagioclase, pyroxene and magnetite
Granitic plutonic rock consisting of quartz, muscovite and alkali feldspar
questions.solution: Kimberlite: diamond-bearing. Pipe-like bodies. South Africa, Siberia.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Himalayan stratigraphy: Tethyan sedimentary sequence:
options: Paleozoic-Mesozoic marine sediments on top of Higher Himalayan Crystalline
Archean gneissic basement forming the core of the Lesser Himalayan belt
Precambrian granite intrusions that cut across the Sub-Himalayan Siwalik belt
Cenozoic volcanic piles interbedded with the Miocene foreland molasse
questions.solution: Tethyan: marine fossiliferous. Folds, thrusts. Overlying Higher Himalayan Crystalline.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: How do chert nodules typically form within limestone sequences?
options: Detrital quartz sand grains washed in from continents and deposited together with the carbonate mud
Silica from sponge spicules, radiolaria. Remobilized by diagenetic fluids. Replaces CaCO₃
Primary mineral precipitation directly from warm seawater without any biological silica contribution
Volcanic ash layers altered to clay, with silica supplied entirely from submarine hydrothermal vents
questions.solution: Chert: biogenic silica. Diagenetic: silicification of limestone. Nodular or bedded.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Andalusite, the low-pressure polymorph of Al2SiO5, characteristically shows which cross-section in contact metamorphic rocks?
options: High-P polymorph of Al2SiO5. Bladed crystals in blueschist and eclogite facies
High-T polymorph of Al2SiO5. Needle-like crystals in granulite facies rocks
Low-P polymorph of Al2SiO5. Square cross-section. Contact metamorphism
Fe-Mg sheet silicate with hexagonal twinning in low-grade slates
questions.solution: Andalusite: low-P, high-T. Chiastolite (cross pattern in section). Hornfels facies.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Resistivity method: Schlumberger array vs Wenner array:
options: Schlumberger uses equal electrode spacings while Wenner is used only for deep soundings
Schlumberger: AB/2 >> MN/2 (deep sounding). Wenner: equal spacing (profiling)
Both arrays give identical results and neither separates sounding from profiling
Wenner: AB/2 >> MN/2. Schlumberger: all four electrodes spaced equally along the line
questions.solution: Schlumberger: vertical sounding. Wenner: horizontal profiling. Schlumberger: fewer electrode moves.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Carbonatite-related REE deposits, such as Bayan Obo and Mountain Pass, originate from which type of magma?
options: Banded iron formation precipitated from Precambrian iron- and silica-rich seawater
Low-temperature carbonate-hosted lead and zinc deposits of the Mississippi Valley type in platform sequences
Bayan Obo (China), Mountain Pass (USA). REE, Nb, P, F. Mantle-derived carbonate magma
Granite-hosted quartz veins enriched in tin and tungsten by late-stage fluids
questions.solution: Carbonatite: LREE enriched. Monazite, bastnasite. ~50% of world REE from carbonatites.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: After 2 half-lives, the percentage of the original radioactive parent isotope remaining is:
questions.solution: Fraction remaining = (1/2)^2 = 25%.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A bed drops 30 m over a horizontal distance of 20 m. Its dip angle is about:
questions.solution: dip = tan⁻¹(rise/run) = tan⁻¹(30/20) ≈ 56.3°.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A coal sample (proximate analysis) has 8% moisture, 25% volatile matter and 20% ash. Its fixed carbon is:
questions.solution: Fixed C = 100 − (moisture + VM + ash) = 100 − (8+25+20) = 47%.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The pump-and-treat method of groundwater remediation involves:
options: Extracts contaminated groundwater and treats it
Injects clean water to force contaminants into a confined zone
Stimulates natural microbes to degrade contaminants in situ
Pumps oxygen into the aquifer to oxidize dissolved metals
questions.solution: Pump-and-treat: extract and treat at surface.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which term describes different minerals having different chemical compositions but the same crystal structure?
options: Same composition in different crystal structures (e.g., diamond, graphite)
Two minerals of identical composition forming in the same habit
Minerals that share the same chemical formula but differ in cleavage
Different compositions, same crystal structure (e.g., olivine series)
questions.solution: Isomorphous series: Fe and Mg substitute in olivine (fayalite-forsterite).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which of the following correctly describes river terraces, including paired versus unpaired forms and their causes?
options: Flat area of the valley floor that is currently flooded every year
Lowest part of the channel occupied by water throughout the year
Abandoned floodplain levels. Paired vs unpaired. Climatic or tectonic
Triangular deposit of sediment formed where a river enters a standing body of water
questions.solution: Terraces: former floodplains. Paired: both sides same level (rapid incision).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In radar remote sensing, a surface that is smooth relative to the wavelength produces which kind of reflection and resulting backscatter?
options: No detectable return, the surface appears completely black
Multiple bounces that enhance the radar backscatter signal
questions.solution: Rough surface: diffuse → high backscatter. Smooth: mirror-like → low return. Water: dark.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which geophysical method involves current injection and vertical electrical sounding?
options: Measures the natural magnetic field of the Earth without any current
Uses ground-penetrating radar pulses to map shallow buried utilities
Detects compressional wave velocities for bedrock depth determination
Current injection. Vertical electrical sounding (VES) for groundwater
questions.solution: Resistivity: Wenner and Schlumberger arrays. Low ρ = water, clay. High ρ = hard rock.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Sequence stratigraphy: flooding surface vs maximum flooding surface:
options: FS: deepest water, MFS: shallowest water and most seaward shoreline position
FS: shallowing-upward break. MFS: deepest water, maximum landward shoreline
MFS: shallowing-upward break, FS: deepest water with condensed deposition
Both surfaces mark exactly the same horizon and are used interchangeably
questions.solution: Flooding surface: parasequence boundary. MFS: maximum transgression. Condensed section.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A migmatite is a partially melted metamorphic rock showing which characteristic banding?
options: Fully melted rock that crystallized into a coarse-grained granite
Sedimentary rock that recrystallized entirely in the solid state with no melt phase involved
Unmelted protolith that retained its original sedimentary layering
Partially melted metamorphic rock. Dark (restite) + light (leucosome) bands
questions.solution: Migmatite: between metamorphism and igneous. Leucosome: granitic melt.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Laterite ore deposits formed by weathering include which correct metal-ore associations?
options: Supergene enrichment of copper beneath the oxidation zone of sulfide deposits
Stratabound manganese beds deposited in shallow marine shelf basins
Hydrothermal vein deposits formed by epithermal hot-spring circulation systems
Bauxite (Al), Ni-laterite (Ni), Fe (Fe), Mn (Mn). Weathering products
questions.solution: Laterite: tropical weathering. Al laterite: gibbsite, boehmite. Ni laterite: saprolite + limonite.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Maceral groups: vitrinite, inertinite, liptinite. Vitrinite originates from:
options: Algal blooms deposited in quiet lacustrine basins
Spores and pollen grains of vascular plants
questions.solution: Vitrinite: from vascular plant tissues. Major maceral in most coals. Reflectance used for rank.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Barchan, transverse, star and parabolic dunes together with loess are landforms created by which agent of erosion and deposition?
options: Cliffs, wave-cut platforms, spits and marine terraces shaped by wave erosion
U-shaped valleys, cirques, arêtes and horns cut by glacier ice
Barchan, transverse, star, parabolic dunes. Loess (wind-blown silt)
Meanders, oxbow lakes and braided reaches shaped by river processes
questions.solution: Barchan: crescent-shaped, horns downwind. Transverse: perpendicular to wind. Loess: fertile soil.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What igneous texture shows large crystals (phenocrysts) set in a fine-grained groundmass?
options: Rock consisting entirely of glass with no crystals visible even under microscope
Uniform texture in which all crystals are fine-grained and of similar size
Coarse texture with all grains large enough to be seen with the naked eye
questions.solution: Porphyritic: two-stage cooling. Phenocrysts form slowly, groundmass quenches.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Garnet zoning profiles: bell-shaped Mn pattern indicates:
options: Diffusion resetting that homogenizes the core composition
Retrograde re-equilibration along fractures during exhumation
Prograde growth zoning (Mn partitioned into garnet early)
Inherited zoning from detrital cores of sedimentary origin
questions.solution: Garnet prograde: high Mn core, decreasing outward (Rayleigh fractionation). Growth zoning.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Quartz (hardness 7) will scratch, but not be scratched by, which mineral?
options: Topaz with a hardness of 8 on the Mohs scale
Corundum which is harder than topaz (9)
questions.solution: A mineral scratches anything softer; quartz (7) scratches feldspar (6) but not topaz/corundum/diamond.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Siwalik Group: Upper Siwalik (Plio-Pleistocene) facies:
options: Marine limestone with abundant coral and foraminiferal remains
Volcanic ash and basalt flows interbedded with the riverine sediments
Glacial till and outwash gravels deposited by valley glaciers
questions.solution: Upper Siwalik: coarse alluvium. Middle: sandstone. Lower: fine sandstone and siltstone.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: To which crystal system does the common salt mineral halite belong?
questions.solution: Halite (NaCl) — cubic crystals. Perfect cubic cleavage.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which are the major Gondwana sedimentary basins distributed across peninsular India?
options: The Himalayan frontal basins of Kashmir and the Karewa lake deposits
The east coast basins like Cauvery and Krishna-Godavari delta areas
The Bengal basin together with the shallow shelf of the Bay of Bengal
questions.solution: Gondwana: rift basins. Lower Gondwana (Permian): coal measures. Upper Gondwana (Triassic-Jurassic): sandstones.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which preprocessing step removes sensor and atmospheric effects and converts digital numbers into radiance and reflectance values?
options: Remove sensor and atmospheric effects. DN → radiance → reflectance. Calibration coefficients
Remove only the terrain shadowing effects, while leaving the sensor and atmospheric noise in the scene uncorrected
Resample the image to a standard map projection using a set of surveyed ground control points
Enhance the contrast of the image to make dark scenes visually interpretable
questions.solution: Radiometric: from raw DN. Radiance: L = Gain·DN + Offset. Reflectance: ρ = π·L·d²/(ESUN·cosθ).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which remote sensing techniques, passive and active, are commonly used to estimate soil moisture from space?
options: Using only optical NDVI vegetation indices, which can directly measure the root-zone water content
Using thermal inertia alone, as derived from a single daytime thermal image only
Passive microwave (L-band: SMOS, SMAP). Active (C-band: Sentinel-1). Optical/thermal
Using only ground-based gravimetry, with no spaceborne sensing involved at all
questions.solution: SMAP: L-band radiometer + radar. 3km, 2-3 day. Soil moisture + freeze/thaw. Surface ~5cm depth.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A bed dipping at 45° shows a width of 40 m across a horizontal surface. Its true (perpendicular) thickness is about:
questions.solution: True thickness = width × sin(dip) = 40×sin45° ≈ 28.28 m.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which option correctly describes how a coastal spit forms and what features develop at its seaward end?
options: Ridge of sand attached to the mainland coast at both of its ends
Block of resistant bedrock rising above the sea surface offshore
Sand/gravel extension from headland. Hook at end. Longshore drift
Long ridge of sand submerged below the water surface parallel to the shore
questions.solution: Spit: continues until across a bay (baymouth bar). Tombolo: connects island to mainland.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: According to Anderson's theory of faulting, which principal stress is vertical in normal, reverse and strike-slip faults, respectively?
options: Normal fault: σ₁ horizontal. Reverse: σ₃ horizontal. Strike-slip: σ₁ vertical
All three fault types form with the same stress orientation and differ only by dip angle
Normal fault: σ₂ vertical. Reverse: σ₁ vertical. Strike-slip: σ₃ vertical
Normal fault: σ₁ vertical. Reverse: σ₃ vertical. Strike-slip: σ₂ vertical
questions.solution: Anderson: σ₁ = maximum principal stress. Orientation of fault depends on which stress is vertical.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A mineral specimen of mass 81 g has a volume of 30 cm³. Its specific gravity is about:
questions.solution: SG = mass/volume = 81/30 = 2.7.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Transmissivity T of an aquifer is expressed by which product and in what units?
options: T = K/b with b the thickness of the aquifer under test
T = K·b (b = aquifer thickness). m²/day or m²/s
T = b/K where b is the saturated thickness of the aquifer
T = K·b² using the aquifer thickness squared in the product
questions.solution: T: production capacity. T > 0.01 m²/s = good aquifer.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A 3 m seam over 6 km² (density 1.4 t/m³) has a recovery factor of 0.6. The mineable reserve is about:
questions.solution: Mineable = area×thickness×density×recovery = 6M m²×3×1.4×0.6 ≈ 15.1 Mt.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In the faulted block shown, the hanging wall has moved down relative to the footwall. This is a:
questions.solution: Hanging wall down = normal fault, caused by extension/tension.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: On the Mohs scale of hardness, the hardest mineral (value 10) is:
questions.solution: Mohs scale runs from talc (1) to diamond (10), the hardest natural mineral.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: How is a paraconformity recognized when no visible erosional surface separates parallel strata?
options: No visible erosional surface. Missing time recognized only by fossils
A visible erosional surface separates tilted older beds from overlying horizontal younger beds
Sedimentary layers rest directly on eroded crystalline igneous or metamorphic basement rocks
An irregular ancient erosion surface separates parallel strata with a clearly visible channel relief
questions.solution: Paraconformity: parallel beds with no obvious erosion. Biostratigraphic gap.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: GIS coordinate systems: projected vs geographic:
options: Geographic: flat coordinates in meters. Projected: spherical coordinates in degrees
Both systems store all of their coordinates in degrees, as measured on a sphere
Projected: latitude and longitude. Geographic: UTM coordinates in meters
Projected: flat (UTM, meters). Geographic: spherical (lat/lon, degrees)
questions.solution: Geographic: WGS84 lat/lon. Projected: UTM (meters). Distortion in projected systems.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In sandstone cement paragenesis, the typical order of cement precipitation from early to late is:
options: All cement types form simultaneously during shallow burial before any significant compaction of the sediment has taken place
Early (calcite, pyrite) → Mesogenetic (quartz overgrowth, illite, ankerite) → Telogenetic (kaolinite, Fe-oxides)
All cements form during deep burial late diagenesis after compaction
Cements precipitate in a random order unrelated to burial history
questions.solution: Paragenesis: diagenetic sequence. Relative timing from cross-cutting and texture.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A rock retains 50% of its original parent isotope (half-life 0.7 Gyr). Its radiometric age is about:
options: 0.7 Gyr (equal to one full half-life of the parent)
questions.solution: 50% remaining ⇒ 1 half-lives ⇒ age = 1×0.7 = 0.7 Gyr.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: An opencast block of 10000 m² has 30 m of overburden above the seam. The overburden volume to be removed is:
questions.solution: Volume = area × depth = 10000×30 = 300000 m³ = 0.3 million m³.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In vorticity analysis, the rotation of rigid porphyroclasts within a ductile matrix is used to assess:
options: Volume change measured from pressure shadows around rigid grains
Temperature of deformation recorded by metamorphic mineral assemblages and growth zoning in porphyroblasts
Strain only, ignoring the rotation of material lines and rigid objects
Porphyroclast rotation. Rigid grains in ductile matrix. Rotational vs non-rotational deformation
questions.solution: Vorticity number W_k: simple shear (1), pure shear (0), general (0-1). Hyperbolic flow.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In an unconfined aquifer, the water table is the boundary between the:
options: Boundary between saturated and unsaturated zones. Fluctuates with recharge
Upper surface of the confining bed that caps the aquifer beneath the zone
Level at which water stands in a well drilled into a confined aquifer body
Zone of permanent saturation that lies below the regional water table surface
questions.solution: Water table: follows topography. Perched water table: above regional water table.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Remote sensing for geology: lineament analysis identifies:
options: Only vegetation density and land use categories
Linear thermal anomalies, not structural geological features
Stream network order and drainage basin boundaries
Faults, fractures, joints, dikes, lithological boundaries
questions.solution: Lineaments: linear features from satellite imagery. Structural control. Mineralization often associated.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The colour of a mineral's powder, seen when it is rubbed on a porcelain plate, is its:
questions.solution: Streak is the colour of the fine powder, often more diagnostic than the surface colour.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: During the recovery phase of a pumping test, residual drawdown s' is given by which formula?
options: Recovery data yield the storage coefficient S but never the value of T
Residual drawdown s' = (2.303Q)/(4πT)·log(t/t'). No S estimate needed
Recovery analysis requires pumping at two different constant discharge rates
Residual drawdown is recorded only during the pumping phase of the test
questions.solution: Recovery: T from slope of s' vs log(t/t'). More reliable than drawdown (constant rate).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Crystal symmetry elements: rotation axes, mirror planes, inversion centers:
options: 14 groups. Symmetry combinations define the fourteen Bravais lattice types
Combination defines point group (32 crystallographic point groups)
7 groups. Each symmetry combination corresponds to one of the seven crystal systems
230 groups. The combinations yield every possible space group for minerals
questions.solution: Point group: symmetry operations. Space group: point group + translations = 230 groups.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: On what basis are arcuate, bird-foot and estuarine deltas classified from one another?
options: Deltas form only where the river dominates over tide and wave
All deltas have identical shapes regardless of sediment supply
Deltas form only where wave action dominates over the river input
questions.solution: Delta: river sediment deposition at coast. Tidal/wave influence shapes delta type.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: SEDEX deposits, formed by exhalation on the seafloor in sedimentary basins, are typically rich in which metals?
options: Volcanic-hosted massive sulfide deposits erupted at mid-ocean ridge spreading centers on the deep seafloor
Alluvial placers enriched by gravity settling of heavy resistant mineral grains
Zn-Pb-Ag deposits in sedimentary basins. Exhalative on seafloor. Broken Hill, McArthur River
Magmatic segregation of chromite and PGE in layered ultramafic intrusions
questions.solution: SEDEX: laminated ore. Reducing basin. Also large tonnage. Bagalkot (India).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Boninite: high-Mg, high-Si volcanic rock. Tectonic setting:
options: Mid-ocean ridge spreading centre with depleted MORB production
Intraplate hot spot chain culminating in a mantle plume axis
Continental rift valley filled with alkaline basalt flows and tuffs
questions.solution: Boninite: MgO>8%, SiO₂>52%, TiO₂<0.5%. Forearc setting. High-T partial melting of hydrated mantle.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The five major Phanerozoic mass extinction events occurred at the end of which periods?
options: A single major event at the end of the Precambrian that removed all shelly faunas
Only two events: the end-Cretaceous asteroid impact and the mid-Pleistocene ice ages
No recognisable pattern, with extinction pulses scattered randomly through every period
questions.solution: P-T extinction: 95% marine species. K-Pg: dinosaurs. End-Ordovician: glaciation.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which twin law produces the polysynthetic twinning diagnostic of plagioclase in thin section?
options: Carlsbad simple twinning that is found only in potassium feldspar minerals
Simple contact twinning developed on the (010) plane
Baveno twinning common in triclinic feldspar varieties
Polysynthetic twinning in plagioclase. Diagnostic in thin section
questions.solution: Albite twinning: repeated lamellae. Characteristic of plagioclase feldspars.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which sub-environments and sedimentary structures characterize the tidal flat depositional environment?
options: Intertidal mudflats dominated by desiccation cracks, evaporite crusts and wind-blown silt, showing a complete absence of marine indicators
Supratidal marsh deposits consisting of laminated organic-rich mud with root traces, gypsum crusts and pyrite framboids, formed exclusively above the high tide line
Subtidal channel sands showing unimodal cross-bedding, gravel lags and a complete absence of mud drapes or bipolar current indicators
Supratidal (marsh), intertidal (mudflat, sandflat), subtidal (channel). Herringbone cross-bedding, flaser bedding, lenticular bedding
questions.solution: Tidal: bipolar cross-bedding (ebb + flood). Mud drapes. Reactivation surfaces.
